revised_claim: Only approximately 4.9–7% of Indonesia's 8–9 million construction workers hold formal competency certifications (SKK/SKA/SKTK). LPJK registry data (December 2024) shows 426,071 registered certified workers out of ~8.76 million construction-sector workers — a rate of ~4.86%. A 2018 Ministry of Public Works Director General statement (citing BPS data) put the rate at ~7% (581,000 certified out of 8.13 million workers). By February 2023 only 411,402 total certificates had ever been issued (Kementerian PUPR). The original 7.4% figure and CIDB/LPJK 2019 attribution is not confirmed by primary sources; current primary-source estimates range from ~4.86% (Dec 2024, LPJK via Ditjen Bina Konstruksi PUPR) to ~7% (2018, PUPR Director General citing BPS). The core assertion — that fewer than 10% of construction workers are formally certified — is well-supported across multiple years and sources.

scope_note: CRITICAL SCOPE DISTINCTION — SKK Konstruksi does NOT cover pressure-part welders for boiler installation. Boiler and pressure vessel welders in Indonesia require SEPARATE specialist certification under Kemnaker RI (Ministry of Manpower) using the K3 Pesawat Uap dan Bejana Tekan framework, rooted in the Steam Act 1930, UU No. 1/1970, and Permenaker No. PER.02/MEN/1982. This K3 certification incorporates ASME Codes (ASME I for boilers, ASME VIII for pressure vessels, ASME Sec. IX for welder performance qualification / WPQ). The SKK Konstruksi system (LPJK/PUPR) covers general construction works such as civil, structural, and building services — not industrial steam boiler welding. For boiler EPC in Southeast Asia, the relevant welder certification bodies are Kemnaker RI (K3 Juru Las, K3 PUBT) and BNSP (through licensed LSPs for welding), sometimes augmented by MIGAS-authority certification for energy installations. The ~5-7% general construction certification rate may therefore UNDERSTATE the shortage for pressure-part welders specifically: the pool qualified for boiler pressure-part welding (Kemnaker/BNSP K3 PUBT pathway) is a much smaller subset of the already-undercertified construction workforce. The original claim's framing using SKK/LPJK as the proxy for boiler-welder certification is technically imprecise but directionally correct: it illustrates a wider structural under-certification problem that is even more acute in the specialist pressure equipment segment.
notes: 1. ORIGINAL FIGURE (7.4%, CIDB/LPJK 2019): Not confirmed by primary sources. The '7.4%' figure appears to originate from a secondary market research aggregator (marketresearchindonesia.com). The CIDB attribution is suspicious — CIDB is a Malaysian body, not Indonesian; the Indonesian equivalent is LPJK. Primary sources show the ~7% figure is a 2018 PUPR Director General statement citing BPS, and more recent LPJK registry data points to ~4.86% as of December 2024. The figure is plausible but the original sourcing chain is broken. 2. TREND: The certification rate has NOT improved materially despite government campaigns. From ~7% in 2018 to ~4.86% in 2024 — the denominator (total construction workers ~8-9M) has grown faster than the numerator (certified workers ~426K-580K). This makes the severity argument stronger, not weaker. 3. WORKFORCE SIZE: Original claim cites '7.62 million' — BPS and PUPR sources suggest the current figure is higher (8.13M per 2018 BPS; 8.76M per Sakernas Aug 2024; ~9.25M per BPS 2023 Construction Statistics). 4. RECOMMENDED REVISION: Replace the precise '7.4%' with a range citing primary sources, update workforce figure, note the ASME/pressure-part scope distinction, and replace CIDB with LPJK/PUPR as the source authority. 5. INTERVIEW RECOMMENDATION: For the most authoritative current figure, contact Direktorat Jenderal Bina Konstruksi (Ditjen Bina Konstruksi) at binakonstruksi.pu.go.id — the directorate publishes periodic SKK registry snapshots. LPJK data portal at lpjk.pu.go.id provides the SIKI registry. For boiler-specific welder certification counts, contact Direktorat Bina K3, Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan (Kemnaker RI).
